source_caption:
A Bronx Tale follows Calogero, a young boy growing up in the Bronx during the 1960s who becomes fascinated by Sonny, a respected local mob boss. As Calogero grows older, he finds himself caught between the honest values taught by his hardworking father and the wealth, power, and influence represented by Sonny.

In A Bronx Tale, the story explores themes of family, loyalty, racism, love, and the difficult choices that shape a person's future. Through Calogero’s journey into adulthood, the film delivers powerful lessons about character and responsibility. Widely praised for its heartfelt storytelling and memorable performances, it remains a beloved coming-of-age crime drama.

source_details.title: A Bronx Tale
source_details.synopsis: A Bronx Tale is a 1993 American coming-of-age crime drama film directed by and starring Robert De Niro in his directorial debut and produced by Jane Rosenthal, adapted from Chazz Palminteri's 1989 one-man play. It tells the coming-of-age story of an Italian-American boy, Calogero, who, after encountering a local Mafia boss, is torn between the temptations of organized crime and the values of his honest, hardworking father, as well as racial tensions in his community. The Broadway production was converted to film with limited changes.
